cards.front: When does a static initializer block run?
cards.back: Once, when the class is loaded — before main() and before any object exists
cards.extra: That is why static blocks can run code before the program's entry point, which was how pre-1.7 code sometimes started without main.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::19 Initializer Block

cards.front: In what order do multiple static blocks execute?
cards.back: In source order, top to bottom, interleaved with static field initialisers
cards.extra: Declaration order is the rule, not the position of main or the constructor.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::19 Initializer Block

cards.front: What can a static block reference?
cards.back: Only static members — no instance fields, and no this
cards.extra: There is no object at class-load time, so an instance reference would have nothing to point at.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: What is the output order for two instance blocks and a constructor?
cards.back: Block 1, block 2, then the constructor body
cards.extra: Both blocks and the constructor are one sequence. Multiple blocks run in source order.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::19 Initializer Block

cards.front: Why use an instance initializer block instead of a constructor?
cards.back: To share initialisation code across several constructors without duplicating it
cards.extra: Every constructor gets the block, so a class with three constructors still has one copy of the common setup.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::19 Initializer Block

cards.front: Which runs first: the parent's initializer blocks or the child's?
cards.back: The parent's — its static blocks at class load, its instance blocks during the super() call
cards.extra: Static initialisation walks up from Object; instance initialisation follows the constructor chain upward.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::19 Initializer Block

cards.front: What is the full initialisation order for creating an object of a subclass?
cards.back: Parent static blocks → child static blocks → parent instance blocks → parent constructor → child instance blocks → child constructor
cards.extra: Static happens once per class; the instance half happens on every new, alternating instance block and constructor body per level.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static vs. Instance Initializer Block in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::19 Initializer Block
